reason: The contribution is a model-free entropy-rate filter for curating synthetic training data, which fits no listed family.
The abstract describes a contrastive multimodal framework but never names the model family of its encoders.
The framework is built around coding LLMs with retrieval augmentation, agents and a VLM critic doing self-reflection.
Pre-training uses multi-parametric brain MRI scans (16,022 scans).
It explains MIL models post hoc without naming the MIL model family.
Besides the solvable model, the method is applied to large-scale neuronal population recordings from mouse visual cortex.
Hit discovery is formalized as a sequential experimental design problem for perturbation experiments.
A posterior model is used for the acquisition function but its family is not named in the text.
Experiments use orthogonality-regularized normalizing flows.
It combines pretrained sequence-structure embeddings with a sequence decoder without naming their family.
The contribution is a visual chain-of-thought reasoning scheme for pretrained vision-language-action models.
A new Mamba architecture is trained end to end for tumor staging and survival prediction without pretraining.
A deep evidential regression framework is used but the network family is not named.
The paper addresses credit assignment for delayed rewards and errors via eligibility traces, a sequential learning problem.
The eligibility traces are explicitly formed by a state-space model.
The contribution is a latent dynamical statistical model with a variational filtering and learning algorithm for neural recordings.
The only named model family is VQ-VAE tokenizers used in the pretraining method.
Beyond simulations, the estimator is applied to real data estimating the age profile of retirement income.
The paper is theoretical with regret and cost guarantees on abstract MDPs and reports no real data.
The paper is a convergence analysis of an algorithm and trains or adapts no model itself.
The contrastive encoder family is not named; only a linear dynamical system on embeddings is described.
The main contribution is a method for evaluating LLMs and their benchmarks via concept-level gaps.
The method applies sparse autoencoders to the internal representations of five open-source LLMs.
The bottleneck is designed to identify which spatial edges matter for a target, an interpretability and discovery goal.
The paper develops and empirically compares new PCA and robust PCA algorithms, a non-neural statistical model.
Controllers are trained on expert policy-trajectory observations and evaluated empirically on generalization, with proof as a supplement.
The benchmark is built from four types of single-cell multi-omics data posed to LLMs.
It adjusts dropout in neural networks across architectural configurations without naming a family.
The framework uses an anatomy-adaptive Vision Transformer.
VLM-based GUI agents act in GUI environments and are trained with RL on trajectories.
The proposed method uses learnable class token queries over image patch tokens; CNN CAM is only prior work.
The framework is fitted to ex vivo recordings of mouse retinal ganglion cell responses.
It uses adaptive deep kernel Gaussian processes, combining a neural feature map with a GP.
The goal is instruction-guided image editing, with Instruct-CLIP used to refine data and train latent diffusion models.
Experiments pre-train LLMs (dense and MoE, 130M to 1.3B) with the proposed optimizer.
It builds on biomedical language models to produce concept embeddings, not on large LLMs.
The main evaluation is online adaptation of wireless receivers to time-varying channel streams.
The contribution is online adaptation via learned latent Bayesian filtering, which fits no listed family.
SlideChat is a vision-language assistant built by instruction-tuning a multimodal LLM.
Spectral representations are said to be learned from visual inputs but the learned model family is not named.
It explains and quantifies LLM prompt sensitivity through interaction decomposition, a robustness and interpretability analysis.
The method is a multimodal diffusion transformer (DiT) built on SD3.5M.
The main point is cutting retrieval latency several-fold relative to MLLM encoding.
The main point is computational efficiency of pan-sharpening via learnable look-up tables.
The learning problem is driven by natural-language feedback and evaluated with LLMs in empirical domains.
The paper concerns agentic benchmarks where agents act on tasks with reward designs.
The method is framed as image-to-image translation evaluated on MRI contrasts and CIFAR-10/ImageNet.
The only named model component is a gated cross-attention fusion module.
The model jointly handles EEG signals and language by feeding EEG tokens into an LLM.
The method targets better-calibrated uncertainty estimates for image registration.
